title: Working at Redwood: Handbook overview, roles & career ladders, benefits, hiring and onboarding, and internal tools guide
author: Sofia Alvarez
body:
Summary

This page is the canonical company handbook entry for Redwood Inference covering key topics for current and incoming employees: what it's like to work here, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and a brief internal tools guide. Use links at the end for deeper, targeted pages. This document is maintained by People Ops; please contact people-ops@redwood.ai for corrections.

1) Working at Redwood — high level

Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on production-grade LLM inference. Our culture emphasizes ownership, pragmatic engineering, customer empathy, and measurable outcomes. We expect all employees to:
- Ship iteratively: prioritize customer impact and observability.
- Communicate clearly: use asynchronous updates in Confluence and Slack; escalate using the oncall/incident playbooks when necessary.
- Be inclusive and candid: feedback is given constructively, and we run frequent calibration sessions to ensure fairness.

Working model and hours
- Hybrid-first: We support remote-first work with optional office days. Teams define core collaboration days.
- Normal working hours: flexible; typical overlap window is 10:00–16:00 local time for cross-team coordination.
- Time-off: accrue according to your contract; follow the Time Off policy page to request leave.

2) Roles and career ladders

Overview: roles at Redwood are grouped into broad families: Engineering (infra, runtime, platform), Product, Research/Applied ML, DevEx, SRE, Security, Sales & Customer Success, People Ops, and Finance. Each family maintains a published career ladder that describes expectations across levels.

Individual contributor (IC) progression (example for Engineering)
- IC1 (New grad / Jr): Focused on learning, shipping well-scoped work, and resolving bugs.
- IC2 (Software Engineer): Owns medium-scope projects, contributes to code reviews, and mentors interns.
- IC3 (Senior): Leads cross-team technical work, defines service-level tradeoffs, and participates in architecture discussions.
- IC4 (Staff): Technical leader across teams, drives system design, and influences roadmap.
- IC5 (Principal/Distinguished): Company-wide technical authority, drives strategic initiatives and external technical representation.

Manager progression
- M1 (Manager): Manages a small team (3–8), owns performance and delivery.
- M2 (Senior Manager): Leads managers or larger programs, influences org-level priorities.
- M3+ (Director/VP): Strategic leadership, cross-functional alignment, and company-level responsibilities.

Promotion and leveling process (summary)
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet: accomplishments, impact metrics, feedback, and updated role expectations.
2. Manager submits packet during a promotion cycle or off-cycle with justification.
3. Calibration panel (peers + HR + managers) reviews evidence against ladder criteria.
4. Committee decision communicated; if approved, compensation and title changes follow.

See the career-ladders repo and the People Ops promotion checklist for templates and timelines.

3) Benefits & perks

Health and wellness
- Medical, dental, and vision plans: multiple tiers; Redwood subsidies the majority of premiums. Enrollment windows: new hires have 30 days from start date.
- Mental health: confidential EAP program and therapy stipends available.
- Parental leave: primary caregiver up to 18 weeks, secondary caregiver up to 8 weeks (see the Parental Leave policy page for details and eligibility).

Financial and retirement
- 401(k) with company match (US employees) and regional equivalents for international hires.
- Competitive equity grants for full-time employees and performance-based refreshes.
- Commuter and dependent care benefits where applicable.

Work and development perks
- Generous learning & development stipend ($1,500/year) for books, courses, and conference attendance.
- Home office stipend for new hires and one-time ergonomic allowance.
- Quarterly team offsites budgeted by managers; company all-hands and hack weeks twice per year.

Other benefits
- Flexible paid time off and company-wide holidays.
- Paid volunteer days.
- Commuter, transit benefits, and discounted coworking allowances in select regions.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy
- Hire for impact and learning velocity. Our interviews assess problem-solving, systems thinking, product sense (when relevant), and collaborative communication. We have a strong commitment to diversity and inclusive hiring; interviewers are trained on bias awareness.

Typical interview loop (engineering example)
1. Recruiter screen (phone/video): role fit and logistics.
2. Technical screen (coding or system-design depending on level).
3. Take-home assignment or architecture exercise (optional by role).
4. Onsite loop (4–6 interviews): includes engineering manager, peers, and cross-functional partners; focuses on coding, design, culture fit, and practical tradeoffs.
5. Hiring committee review and offer.

Offer and onboarding
- Offers are extended by People Ops and include compensation, equity, and expected start date. Offers must pass the compensation approval workflow.
- Pre-boarding checklist (completed by People Ops): IT account creation (Okta), 1Password access, laptop order, payroll setup, benefits enrollment link, and first-day schedule.

First 90 days (onboarding milestones)
- Day 0–1: account access, hardware setup, HR orientation, meet your buddy and manager.
- Week 1: team onboarding, codebase walkthrough, first small deliverable, and security training.
- Month 1: owning a small feature/bug, 30-day check-in with manager.
- Month 2: ramp into larger scope, begin cross-team collaboration.
- Month 3: 90-day review, update your 30/60/90 plan, and plan for first performance goals.

Buddy system and mentorship
- Every new hire is assigned a buddy for the first 30 days and a mentor for the first 6 months. Buddies help with tooling, calendar norms, and quick context. Mentors help with career development and technical growth.

5) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

Core collaboration and identity
- Confluence: canonical documentation and runbooks. Create pages in the appropriate space. Use the doc template library for PRDs, runbooks, and ADRs.
- Slack: primary team communication. Public channels for project transparency; use threads and reactions to surface consensus.
- Okta / SSO: primary identity provider. Use single sign-on for all cloud apps.
- 1Password: company password manager; ensure your vault is shared with people-ops and your manager for onboarding.

Engineering and delivery
- GitHub: source control; use branch-per-feature and PR reviews. Follow the Engineering PR checklist.
- CI/CD: pipelines are in the ci-cd-and-build space; refer to pipeline conventions and release notes for tagging and versioning.
- Staging & Prod clusters: access requires MFA and approved role-based access. Follow the runbook before running disruptive changes.
- Issue tracking: Linear is used for triage and sprints (Jira where applicable for some enterprise projects).

Observability & incident response
- Redwood Console: primary metrics, tracing, and log dashboards. Use per-route dashboards for latency/cost visibility.
- PagerDuty/Oncall: oncall rotations are managed by SRE. Follow the oncall runbook when paged.

How to request access or raise an IT ticket
- Automated access requests: submit via the Access & Permissions page or the IT service form.
- Emergency access: use the oncall SRE channel in Slack and the escalations playbook for urgent infra issues.

6) Policies and practical guidance

Performance reviews and feedback cycles
- We run semi-annual performance cycles with mid-cycle calibration. Career conversations happen continuously; managers should schedule 1:1s at least weekly for new hires.
- Feedback: use structured feedback forms and 360 inputs for promotion and comp cycles.

Security and data handling
- All employees must complete security awareness training within 7 days of start. Sensitive data access requires an approved business justification and least-privilege access.

How to find more detailed pages
- Career ladders and promotion templates: see the career-ladders page in People Ops.
- Benefits details and plan documents: Benefits & Enrollment page (include region-specific guides).
- Hiring and interview training: Interviewer training and hiring committee guidelines page.
- Onboarding checklists and templates: Onboarding -> New Hire Checklist page.
